title: Paired SPHEREx measurements retain the 2025 band of Gaia20cdd under a bounded extinction model
abstract: SPHEREx builds spectra over time. We test whether brightness changes can cause the reported 3.1 um depression of Gaia20cdd. We fit 24 simultaneous detector pairs in two 2025 visits, with a free true short-wavelength brightness in every exposure. We test 21 long-to-short extinction ratios from zero to one and linear and quadratic continua. With a 0.04 ratio error floor, fitted depths remain 0.284-0.337 in July and 0.388-0.421 in December. The short-wavelength monitor has no measured feature of the same shape. Propagating monitor errors reduces the July amplitude/error statistic to about 2.3 at the largest extinction ratio. December gives 4.56 or 2.85 for the two continua. The result limits a time-scan explanation within a fixed extinction-ratio model. It also limits claims that both visits independently exceed three formal errors. Shared calibration, an unknown stellar reference, inherited QR2 wavelengths and model-dependent errors prevent a false-alarm or water-ice identification claim. Code, input hashes, fit summaries, figures and synthetic checks permit reproduction from the signed source.
